[1-3]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “noise and tumult” of life, seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul, or are you looking for a “rule of life” that prioritizes the “external Word” over the “subjective feelings” of our digital age? [4-8]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos,” we must return to the “divine handbook” to see how the Lord personally governs our growth through the disciplined saturation of His Word [4, 9-11].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the organization of your time—by day, month, and year—is a stewardship intended to “conform your desires and purposes to His will and glory” [8, 12, 13].

***

### **Section 1: The Daily Rhythm of God-Consciousness**

**Verse**
“ ‘This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success’ ” (Joshua 1:8). [14-16]. “ ‘But His delight is in the law of the LORD, and in His law he meditates day and night’ ” (Psalm 1:2). [16-19].

**Meaning**
The sources provide a “daily reading habit” designed to develop “continual God consciousness,” where every thought becomes an opportunity to commune with the Father [5, 20-22]. This daily structure is organized through four distinct portions of Scripture each day: a section from the Old Testament, one from the Psalms, one from Proverbs, and one from the New Testament [22, 23]. The “sole objective” is to “saturate and renew your mind” so that the Word of God “dominates your attitudes and actions” from the moment you rise until you lie down [24-26]. This is not a “meaningless repetition” but a “total way of life” [4, 27].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by the idea that a brief, spasmodic reflection is enough to sustain you, for “ ‘man shall not live by bread alone; but man lives by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD’ ” (Deuteronomy 8:3) [4, 28-33]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” and you must “discipline your mind” to “dwell on whatever things are true,” for “as [a person] thinks within himself, so he is” (1 Corinthians 6:19; Philippians 4:8; Proverbs 23:7) [34-39].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “Shema” (Deuteronomy 6:4–9) was a “formalized prayer” repeated twice daily as a “temporal sign” of loyalty to the theocracy [40-44]. The New Testament **revises** this by revealing that “true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth,” meaning our daily devotion is not a “ritualized ceremony” but a “spiritual service of worship” involving the “renewing of your mind” (John 4:23; Romans 12:1–2) [40, 44-50].

***

### **Section 2: The Monthly Deep-Dive and Check-In**

**Verse**
“ ‘And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God’ ” (Romans 12:2). [46, 51, 52]. “ ‘As newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby’ ” (1 Peter 2:2). [53-57].

**Meaning**
The sources offer a “monthly check-in framework” through a unique plan for the New Testament: reading one book repetitiously for an entire month [58]. For example, one might read 1 John every day for 30 days to develop a “visual perception of the book” in the mind [58]. Longer books, like the Gospel of John, are divided into three sections of seven chapters each, allowing for a three-month intensive study [59]. This method ensures that the “Word of Christ [dwells] in you richly,” transforming your character month by month into the “image of the One who created him” (Colossians 3:10, 16) [60-64].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust” in the Spirit’s power to change you, for “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6) [37, 65-72]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” evaluating each month whether your life is producing “fruit in keeping with repentance” (1 Corinthians 9:27; Matthew 3:8) [34, 40, 67, 73-78].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, the “New Moon” was a monthly feast and “sabbatical” time of assembly [79-81]. The New Testament **revises** our calendar of holiness, showing that “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ,” so that we find our “repose of the soul” in His Word rather than in a “moon or any of the host of heaven” (Hebrews 4:10; Colossians 2:16–17; Deuteronomy 17:3) [40, 44, 45, 50, 82-91].

***

### **Section 3: The Quarterly Framework (The 52-Week Key Passages)**

**Verse**
“ ‘For the word of God is living and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart’ ” (Hebrews 4:12). [92, 93]. “ ‘Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints!’ ” (Revelation 15:3). [94].

**Meaning**
The sources contain “quarterly review prompts” through a section spotlighting 52 key Scripture passages, designed to be studied one per week for a year [24, 95, 96]. These passages are grouped into seasonal themes such as “The Sovereignty and Character of God” (Weeks 1–13), “The Nature of Man and Sin” (Weeks 14–26), “The Person and Work of Christ” (Weeks 27–39), and “The Spiritual Life and the Future Kingdom” (Weeks 40–52) [587–634]. This quarterly structure acts as a “soldier’s sword” to “unmask our hypocrisy” and “build us up” in the faith [93, 97].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” using these quarterly anchors to ensure you are “not tossed to and fro... by the trickery of men” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Ephesians 4:14) [8, 10, 27, 68, 83, 98-112]. You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge,” for these core truths are “able to make you wise for salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus” (2 Timothy 3:15) [113-118].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Stewardship**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the “Feasts of the Lord” were organized seasonally (Firstfruits in Spring, Tabernacles in Fall) to commemorate “national greatness” [42, 44, 119-121]. The New Testament **revises** these seasons, revealing that “Christ fulfills Israel’s feasts,” where our true “Harvest” is the “furtherance of the gospel” and our true “Tabernacle” is the “spirit of the Lord” (1 Corinthians 5:7–8; Philippians 1:12; 2 Corinthians 3:17) [44, 121-128].

***

### **Section 4: The Yearly Reflection and Life Goal**

**Verse**
“ ‘While the earth remains, Seedtime and harvest, Cold and heat, Winter and summer, And day and night Shall not cease’ ” (Genesis 8:22). [129, 130]. “ ‘Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth’ ” (2 Timothy 2:15). [131-135].

**Meaning**
The sources provide a “yearly reflection guide” through the “Bible in one year” schedule, which takes the believer from “creation to consummation, eternity past to eternity future” [136-138]. This yearly journey is hung on “5 recurring motifs” or hooks: 1) The Character of God; 2) Divine Judgment for Sin; 3) The Blessedness of Obedience; 4) The Savior’s Sacrifice; and 5) The Coming Kingdom and Glory [138-140]. At year’s end, the believer reflects on “what He planned for you, why He made you... and what He has prepared for you in eternal glory” [140].

**Takeaway**
“Your life is not your own,” and at the end of each year, you must ask if you are “walking in a manner worthy of the Lord, to please Him in all respects” (Colossians 1:10; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [34, 37-39, 45, 74, 141-143]. Recognize that “heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away,” and therefore your “sole objective” should be to “lay your life on God’s altar as a living sacrifice” (Matthew 24:35; Romans 12:1) [46, 74, 98, 111, 144-154].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, the “Year of Jubilee” every 50 years was a time to “proclaim liberty throughout all the land” [128, 155, 156]. The New Testament **revises** our vision of time, showing that “now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation,” because the “Heir of all things” has already obtained “eternal redemption” for us (2 Corinthians 6:2; Hebrews 1:2; 9:12) [44, 112, 157-159].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [4, 10, 38, 68, 93, 103, 116, 160-178].

On over 125 occasions, Leviticus indicts mankind for uncleanness and/or instructs on how to be purified.
